$schema-note: v1.0.0-recovery-testing skip-enforcement manifest (design.md §1.1, Task 0.4). This is the AUTHORITATIVE required set: 'required' lists the stable id of EVERY non-live crash/soak test that MUST execute-and-pass in the required gate (G9). check-required-tests.ts fails the gate by id if any required id is missing or reported skipped/todo/failed. 'deferred' lists WHERE-gated optional-feature ids that reconcile as skipped-pending-feature and are exempt while their feature is unshipped. Each governed test embeds its id as a [[id]] token in its title (which Vitest surfaces in assertionResults[].title/fullName). The Task-0 crash-harness smoke ids (crash-harness.smoke.*) plus the full T1/T2/T5/T3/soak/load-under-prune/P3 id set below form the contract that Tasks 1-6 tag their tests with; the ids are defined NOW so later tasks adopt them verbatim without a spec rewrite. CHANGE-LEVEL AUDIT (BLOCK 9): check-required-tests.ts now FAILS CLOSED (a missing/unparseable/empty-or-absent required set fails the gate, never reconciles as 'all 0 passed'), STRUCTURALLY PINS required.length to EXPECTED_REQUIRED_COUNT (currently 29 -- 25 from v1.0.0-recovery-testing plus the four 00009-01 archive per-height atomicity ids) so silently deleting or adding a required entry fails the gate, and BINDS each required id to its 'file' so an id that executed-and-passed from a DIFFERENT file (a token moved to a trivial passing test) fails. The co-transactional saveAndAdvance crash test (crash.saveAndAdvance.co-tx-atomic, BLOCK 1) is required entry #23; the change-level round-3 differential negative-control (BLOCK 3) and reference import-clean (BLOCK 4) guards are required entries #24 and #25; every required entry MUST carry its bound 'file'. 42 -> 45 (00009-06): three ids for the operator surface — the list's revoked/deleted membership asymmetry, the dashboard's self-containment (no external resource, with a positive control), and the derive-key command agreeing byte-for-byte with the service's own key encoding.
$check-mechanism-note: IMPORTANT: run against the CURRENT Task-0-only suite, check-required-tests.ts will correctly report the not-yet-built required ids (the crash.* / soak.* / property.p3.* entries) as `missing` — those tests are authored by Tasks 1-6. That is EXPECTED and correct: check-required-tests.ts is the G9 RELEASE gate, green only once every task has landed its tagged tests. The check MECHANISM itself is proven independently, right now, by the synthetic-payload unit tests in check-required-tests.test.ts (which use an inline manifest, not this file), so those unit tests stay green regardless of how many required ids are still unbuilt. Do NOT delete a required id to make the check pass early — that would re-open the exact self-skip hole this manifest closes.

required.description: 0.1: spawn the crash worker, SIGKILL it, confirm the shared container is still up and a fresh client connects.
0.1: pg_terminate_backend drops a targeted backend's connection and the dedicated pool recovers (reconnects with a new backend pid).
0.3: a query against a deliberately-stalled backend is bounded by a 1.5s override of the suite watchdog and throws a typed SuiteWatchdogTimeoutError before G7's 120s, not a hang.
0.3: withSuiteWatchdog with NO explicit override applies SUITE_WATCHDOG_MS as its default bound (proven fast via fake timers, so the default is wired without a real 60s wait).
0.2: without UMBRADB_CRASH_HOOK the worker performs an ordinary uninterrupted save and exits 0.
0.2: the before-commit hook pauses after the manifest INSERT is issued, before COMMIT, and emits its readiness signal (incl. the worker backend pid); nothing is visible.
0.2: the in-critical-section hook pauses inside a held withLease; exactly one class-2 advisory lock with objid = hashtext(leaseKey) is held.
0.2: the after-data-commit-before-cursor hook runs TWO real ops (save then cursor) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves data durable and the cursor absent (watermark behind data).
0.2: the after-cursor-before-data hook runs TWO real ops (cursor then save) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves the cursor durable and the data absent (T5 unsafe reference case).

0.2 (test-honesty): the SAME co-transactional data->cursor flow run to completion WITHOUT a kill lands BOTH data and cursor — the negative control proving the killed T5 runs' absences are caused by the crash, not by a missing op.

T1 (Task 1.1): SIGKILL at before-commit leaves no complete=true manifest at the interrupted seq; the prior seq still loads+hash-verifies; no orphan junction rows; negative control (no kill => visible complete manifest).

T2 (Task 2.1): Postgres killed mid-save => the in-flight save rejects with a typed ConnectionError (not a raw driver error); after recovery the checkpoint is all-or-nothing and load(latest) returns correct bytes.

T2 (Task 2.2): the lost-COMMIT-ack state built by the sanctioned simulation (a provably-committed save re-invoked with identical content) yields a benign identical-content duplicate at the next seq; load(latest) correct either way; static check that save is excluded from any auto-retry allowlist.

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): killed at after-data-commit-before-cursor, the durable watermark is never ahead of durable data (every write batch with cursor <= durable watermark is present in durable data).

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): replay from the durable cursor converges on a current state equal (current-state equality predicate: kv_current + latest complete checkpoint payload + watermark values; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference replay of the same write-batch sequence.
T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): the watermark-never-ahead invariant holds under synchronous_commit = on.

T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): under synchronous_commit = off with an UNCLEAN postmaster kill (pg_ctl stop -m immediate / in-container kill -9), a lost tail of acknowledged commits is acceptable but an inverted durability order (cursor durable, data not) is a failure.
T3 (Task 4.1): after a lease-holder is SIGKILLed, a fresh process's withLease on the same key acquires immediately (bounded wait, no wedge) and pg_locks shows the class-2 advisory lock gone.

Soak (Task 5.1): a sustained concurrent mix at a declared envelope (10^5-10^6 chunks) samples a named P1-P10-derived SQL-observable invariant set DURING the run (gapless per-key version, only complete manifests loadable, no dangling junction, watermark <= max durable data); end state equals a fault-free reference; each GC-pass duration is recorded and bounded by GC_PASS_WATCHDOG_MS (no perf threshold gates).

Load-under-prune (Task 5.2): a FORCED, verified interleave lands the prune COMMIT inside load's open REPEATABLE READ snapshot window; load returns correct bytes and never raises ChunkIntegrityError/ChunkMissingError for a surviving checkpoint; negative control (un-snapshotted read of a reclaimed chunk DOES raise ChunkMissingError) fires.

P3 anchor (Task 6.1): the existing P3 replay/fold-equivalence property (getAt matches a from-scratch fold of the put sequence) is the differential gate's fold-equivalence anchor, satisfied WITHOUT importing the replaced store. Task 6.1 tags the existing P3 test with this id; no new test code.

Differential fault-schedule (Task 6.2, depends on G5): a SEEDED (reproducible, no Math.random) schedule mixing the G9 faults T1/T2/T5 across write batches, re-syncing from durable state after each fault, converges to a current state EQUAL (current-state predicate: full kv_current + full watermarks + latest complete checkpoint payload; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference run (a replay via UmbraDB's own adapters — NOT reference-merge.ts, which is transaction-history-merge only; no foreign consumer/indexer import, verified by an in-test import audit) of the same schedule. Mandatory negative control: a deliberately-broken variant that drops a committed range makes the equivalence assertion FIRE.

Co-transactional G5 crash (change-level audit BLOCK 1): saveAndAdvance — the single-transaction save+cursor combinator — SIGKILLed BETWEEN its internal checkpoint-data write and its cursor write (both inside the ONE uncommitted tx, paused via a test-only query observer over saveAndAdvance's own sql, NO src change) leaves NEITHER the checkpoint NOR the watermark advance durable (all-or-nothing), and a fresh saveAndAdvance on the same key then lands seq 1 committing both; a no-kill co-tx-full-flow control lands BOTH. Crash-tests G5 atomicity DIRECTLY (the two-transaction T5 tests never crash saveAndAdvance itself).

Differential negative control (change-level round-3 BLOCK 3): the mandatory dropped-range negative control - a deliberately-broken variant that skips one faulted batch's recovery so a committed range is genuinely dropped - makes the SAME current-state equality predicate the positive test relies on FIRE (throw). Required-enforced so deleting/skipping the control (or weakening assertCurrentStateEqual) turns the gate red by id.

Differential reference import-cleanliness (change-level round-3 BLOCK 4): a static audit that the in-repo reference imports nothing outside the repo - directly AND through its relative-import closure - catching bare import, dynamic import() and require(), and rejecting any @midnightntwrk/indexer/consumer/wallet specifier. Required-enforced so skipping/removing it turns the gate red by id.

00009-01 / owner Rule A (spec/00009 FR-029): 200 randomized PostgreSQL kills inside the per-height archive transaction leave exactly {nothing of H, all of H incl. watermark}; both classes must occur (non-vacuity) and every interrupted height must re-commit whole on retry.

00009-01 / owner Rule A: a real child writer process SIGKILLed at named statement indices inside the per-height transaction leaves nothing of H; SIGKILLed immediately after the commit returned it leaves all of H including the watermark.

00009-01 test-honesty control: the PRE-FOLD three-transaction shape (bundle, then checkpoint, then watermark) DOES expose a partial height, so the two-state result above is caused by the fold rather than by assertions that cannot fail.
00009-01: the transactional progress NOTIFY is delivered for a committed height and never for a rolled-back one, so a listener may treat an arrival as 'this height is readable'.

00009-02 (organizer spec FR-012, US3 scenario 1): a pause landing between a worker's load and its commit fences the advance, and a stale epoch commits nothing -- asserted with a full-content snapshot of every shielded_monitor table before and after, plus a positive control proving the same batch DOES commit under the current epoch.

00009-02 (owner Rule B, organizer spec US5 scenario 4 / FR-025): the whole project-B flow runs as a PostgreSQL role holding only USAGE+SELECT on chain_archive, and the seeded archive content is byte-identical afterwards; a positive control asserts that same role's direct archive write IS rejected, so the boundary is real.

00009-02 (organizer spec FR-024): real pg_dump snapshot -> revoke -> DROP SCHEMA -> psql restore -> re-apply the exported revocation list; the monitor is refused again and an advance against it is fenced. Asserts mid-drill that the restore genuinely lost the revoke, so the drill cannot pass vacuously.

00009-03 / owner Rule B (spec/00009 FR-010, US5 scenario 2): 200 randomized PostgreSQL kills inside the scanner's per-batch transaction leave exactly {no association of H and coverage below H, all of H and coverage H}; both classes must occur, an interrupted height WITH matches and one WITHOUT must both occur (the latter is the case that turns entirely on coverage), and every interrupted batch must redo whole with no duplicate (height, position).

00009-03 / owner Rule B: a real child scanner process SIGKILLed at named statement indices inside its advance transaction leaves nothing of H; SIGKILLed immediately after the commit returned it leaves all of H including coverage. The worker's own pause signal is asserted, so a point that fell past the end of the transaction cannot masquerade as a crash point.

00009-03 test-honesty control: the UNFOLDED shape (associations written, coverage advanced afterwards) DOES expose a partial batch, so the two-state result above is caused by the single transaction rather than by assertions that cannot fail.

00009-03 / owner Rule B, US5 scenario 4: every statement the scanner issues is captured and the ones whose LEADING verb writes are checked to name only shielded_monitor tables, in a run that demonstrably also read the archive. Two positive controls: an archive INSERT is classified and flagged, and a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is NOT classified as a write (so the detector is precise, not merely permissive).

00009-03 / SC-001: end to end over a real archive, every monitor's stored associations equal test/fixtures/shielded-monitor/corpus.manifest.json exactly -- every positive once (including the fallible-segment-only positive and the two-matching-output transaction, which yields ONE row), zero negatives, correct matched segments, appliedOutcome unknown, full FR-009 provenance, gapless seq in (blockHeight, position) order.

00009-03 / FR-013, US5 scenario 5: a re-bootstrapped archive (same chain, new archive instance id) moves the monitor to stale_source with its coverage frozen, instead of silently mixing two histories.

00009-03 / FR-007: an undecodable transaction stops the monitor at its (height, position) with state failed and coverage left BELOW that height -- the unreadable range is never recorded as scanned-and-empty.

00009-04 (organizer spec FR-019, SC-006 analogue for the API): paging the private API's matches endpoint from an empty cursor with limit=5 over 37 associations seeded through the store -- deliberately handed to the store OUT of order -- visits every association exactly once, in (blockHeight, position) order, and the concatenation equals what the store holds. Guards the cursor's exactly-once property, which is what a consumer's whole polling loop rests on.

00009-04 (organizer spec FR-023, SC-004): after every endpoint has been exercised with one dedicated key -- including four failing registrations, one of them the same key bytes encoded for the WRONG network -- every captured log record and every captured response body is scanned for the Bech32m string, its data part, and the serialized bytes in hex/base64/base64url, and finds zero. Carries the mandatory POSITIVE CONTROL: the same scan over a string that really contains the key must find it, so a scanner that looked at the wrong strings cannot pass.

00009-04 (organizer spec SC-008, US1-US3): the reference consumer CLI drives register -> status -> poll(empty) -> poll(matches) -> poll(idempotent resume) -> pause -> resume -> revoke -> delete against a REAL HTTP server on a loopback socket backed by Testcontainers PostgreSQL, asserting state, coverage and cursor-file stability at each step, and that no viewing key appears in anything the client printed. Matches are seeded through the store because Phase 3's scanner does not exist yet; the Compose run with a real shielded transaction is deferred to Phase 5.

00009-06: GET /v1/monitors lists a revoked monitor (whose own reads answer 410) and never lists a deleted one (US3 scenario 4). The documented asymmetry of the operator list; both halves fail silently if broken.

00009-06: the served dashboard references no absolute or protocol-relative URL and declares no subresource-loading attribute, with a positive control. The 'no new runtime dependency, no external resource' constraint as an assertion rather than a review habit.

00009-06: umbradb-shielded-monitor-derive-key produces, for a given seed, exactly the Bech32m string the repository's own fixture path produces — so the command and the service's key intake cannot diverge.
